skill.name: azure-ai-transcription-py

skill.summary: Use Azure AI Transcription from Python for batch and real-time speech-to-text workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, placeholder Azure URLs, and legitimate environment variable examples. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or malicious command execution was found in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 15-17 are a Markdown bash code block showing a normal pip install command. The skill file does not execute this command or interpolate user input into a shell.
Line 17 is the closing Markdown fence for the installation example. It is documentation syntax, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.
Line 21 begins a Markdown code block that lists environment variable names. It is not executable code and contains no command invocation.
Line 24 is the closing Markdown fence for the environment variable example. It does not perform command execution.
Line 30 starts a Markdown Python example for constructing an Azure transcription client. The snippet does not launch external commands.
Line 38 is the closing Markdown fence for the Python authentication example. It is static documentation, not executable shell syntax.
Line 42 starts a Markdown Python example for a batch transcription job. The code demonstrates SDK usage and does not invoke a shell.
Line 51 is the closing Markdown fence for the batch transcription example. It is not an execution primitive.
Line 55 starts a Markdown Python example for real-time streaming transcription. The snippet reads an audio file through the SDK and does not execute external commands.
The URL is a placeholder Azure Cognitive Services endpoint used to show required configuration. It is not a real external collection endpoint or hidden network destination.
The content URL is a placeholder for user-owned audio storage in a batch transcription example. No fixed third-party domain or exfiltration target is present.
The endpoint environment variable is read as normal SDK configuration for the Azure client. There is no evidence it is logged, transmitted elsewhere, or misused.
The transcription key is used as the credential argument for the Azure client. The file does not print, store, or send the key to an unrelated destination.

content.value_statement: Speech projects need accurate setup guidance for Azure batch jobs, streaming, timestamps, and diarization. This skill provides focused Python SDK guidance for implementation planning and usage patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure AI Transcription Python package.
Explains endpoint and key environment variable setup.
Demonstrates subscription key authentication for TranscriptionClient.
Outlines batch transcription with content URLs and diarization.
Outlines real-time transcription from a local audio file.
Highlights timestamps, language selection, backpressure, and session cleanup.
limitations: Does not provide Azure credentials, storage accounts, or audio files.
Does not run transcription jobs or upload audio by itself.
Uses placeholder endpoint and storage URLs that users must replace.
States that DefaultAzureCredential is not supported for this client.

use_cases.title: Prototype speech-to-text in Python
use_cases.description: Developers can plan the package setup, client authentication, and first transcription workflow before writing application code.

use_cases.title: Process long meeting recordings
use_cases.description: Data teams can use batch transcription guidance for stored audio files with speaker diarization and timestamps.

use_cases.title: Add live caption workflows
use_cases.description: Product teams can explore real-time streaming patterns for captions, call notes, and assistive transcription features.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up Azure AI Transcription for a Python project. Include package installation, required environment variables, and client authentication steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a batch job
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a batch transcription flow for meeting recordings stored in Azure storage. Include locale selection, diarization, timestamps, and result handling.

prompt_templates.title: Compare batch and streaming
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Azure AI Transcription batch jobs and real-time streaming for my support call product. Recommend when to use each approach.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my production plan for Azure AI Transcription in Python. Check authentication, storage URLs, error handling, backpressure, cleanup, and privacy controls.

output_examples.input: I need to transcribe stored meeting audio with speaker labels.
output_examples.output: Use a batch transcription job with a user-owned audio URL, set the meeting locale, enable diarization, and collect timestamps from the completed result.

output_examples.input: I need live captions from a local audio source.
output_examples.output: Use a streaming transcription session, send audio in controlled chunks, handle returned text events, and close the session when transcription ends.

output_examples.input: I need help choosing credentials for the client.
output_examples.output: Use the transcription endpoint and subscription key from environment variables. Do not hardcode secrets in source files or shared prompts.

best_practices: Store Azure endpoints and keys in environment variables or a secret manager.
Enable diarization when recordings include multiple speakers.
Specify the expected language and close streaming sessions after use.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode subscription keys in source files or prompts.
Do not use batch transcription for latency-sensitive live captioning.
Do not ignore streaming backpressure during real-time audio uploads.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you plan Azure AI Transcription workflows in Python for batch and real-time speech-to-text use cases.

faq.question: Does it include credentials?
faq.answer: No. You must provide your own Azure endpoint and transcription key through environment variables or a secret manager.

faq.question: Can it transcribe long audio files?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance recommends batch transcription for long files stored at accessible audio URLs.

faq.question: Can it support multiple speakers?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples mention diarization for recordings that include more than one speaker.

faq.question: Does it support DefaultAzureCredential?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that this client uses subscription key authentication instead.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
